sources.title: Directive 2004/38/EC on the right of Union citizens and their family members to move and reside freely
sources.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex publishes the Directive in the Official Journal of the European Union.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No entry visa or equivalent formality may be imposed on Union citizens.

sources.title: EEA-Lex factsheet for Directive 2004/38/EC
sources.officialityEvidence: EFTA's official EEA-Lex identifies the EEA Joint Committee decision and legal status of incorporated EEA acts.
sources.supportingExcerpt: EU legal act incorporated into the EEA Agreement by a Joint Committee Decision.

sources.title: Agreement between the European Community and its Member States and Switzerland on the free movement of persons
sources.publisher: Official Journal of the European Union
sources.officialityEvidence: The agreement is published in the Official Journal and hosted by EUR-Lex, the EU Publications Office legal repository.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The Contracting Parties shall allow nationals of the other Contracting Parties to enter their territory simply upon production of a valid identity card or passport.

sources.title: Convention establishing the European Free Trade Association (Vaduz Convention), updated 1 November 2021
sources.officialityEvidence: EFTA hosts the consolidated Vaduz Convention text as an official legal document.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Freedom of movement of persons shall be secured among Member States.

sources.title: Swiss SEM: Entry without visa
sources.officialityEvidence: Swiss federal State Secretariat for Migration entry guidance on the official sem.admin.ch domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: EU or EFTA citizens must present valid personal identification, an ID card or a passport.

sources.title: Swiss SEM factsheet: Free Movement of Persons with the European Union
sources.officialityEvidence: Swiss federal SEM factsheet published on its official document domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No permit is needed for stays in Switzerland lasting less than three months, either as a tourist.

conditions: This is a same-country citizenship normalization, not a cross-border free-movement rule.
It does not determine passport, identity-card, residence, family-member, public-policy, or territory rules for any other person or destination.

policies.title: EU/EEA passports to Austria: cross-border free movement
policies.summary: Nationals of the listed EU and EEA states may enter Austria under cross-border free-movement rules.
conditions: Limited to nationals of a listed state other than Austria; the Austrian-national pair is separately normalized as citizenship.
For up to three months, the free-movement baseline requires a valid identity card or passport and no entry visa; longer residence is conditional and may require registration.
Third-country family members, residents, refugee/alien documents, and other non-EU/EEA passports are not included; their derived rights and visa requirements must be assessed separately.
Rights may be restricted on public-policy, public-security, or public-health grounds; this country-code policy does not determine overseas, associated, or other non-national territory.
